response.rationale: R7 is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and ventricle, and a hypoplastic left ventricle, which are characteristic of Tetralogy of Fallot. R3, Double Outlet Right Ventricle, is a close runner-up but lacks some key features of Tetralogy of Fallot.

rejected.why: Ebstein's Anomaly does not typically present with two great vessels arising from the right ventricle
Atrial septal defect is not consistent with the presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
Tricuspid Atresia typically presents with a more severe reduction in right ventricular size and a more pronounced left ventricular hypertrophy
Ventricular septal defect is not consistent with the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle and severe tricuspid regurgitation
Tricuspid regurgitation is a feature of the presentation, but it is not a diagnosis that encompasses all of the described findings
